metadata.title: Need-supportive teaching is associated with reading achievement via intrinsic motivation across eight cultures

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for reading (15-year-olds) and applies PISA’s complex two-stage sampling design. The authors state that PISA provides 80 replicate weights plus a final weight, and they compute estimates using plausible values together with the replicate weights to obtain unbiased statistical estimates. In the SEM stage, they explicitly treat the clustered (students within schools) structure using PISA weights and replicates, and they refit models using a pooled within-cluster covariance matrix to account for the sampling design. The manuscript does not report the exact weight variable name(s) from the dataset, but it indicates that the embedded PISA replicate-weight scheme was used as recommended in the PISA analysis manual.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used publicly available PISA 2018 reading-focused data for 15-year-old students across 79 countries/regions, then excluded Canada, Lebanon, and Northern Macedonia because they lacked data on key study variables. The remaining analytic sample comprises 578,168 students across 76 regions, which were grouped into Schwartz’s (2009) eight cultural value orientation groups. The study does not further restrict by grade beyond PISA’s 15-year-old target population, and it reports that missingness on study variables was <6% per case before imputation.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (15-year-olds), Schwartz eight cultural groups (76 regions)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM path estimates (Model 2 with covariates): INT ➔ ACH standardized paths ranged from 0.24 to 0.42 across groups; NST ➔ ACH direct paths were small and varied (e.g., 0.06 in Western Europe; 0.00 in East Central Europe; −0.02 in Africa & Middle East). Indirect effect (NST ➔ INT ➔ ACH) was statistically significant across all eight groups with small effect sizes (e.g., 0.03–0.07). Model fit indices reported as excellent (Table 2A) with robust CLI/TLI and RMSEA values within acceptable ranges.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading the study leveraged reading intrinsic motivation, need-supportive teaching (NST), and covariates (gender and SES) to predict reading achievement (Plausible Values), finding that intrinsic motivation had the strongest positive association with achievement across all eight cultural groups while the direct effect of NST on achievement was only partially supported (not supported in East-Central Europe and Africa & Middle East). This indicates that policies aiming to improve reading outcomes should prioritize fostering students’ intrinsic reading motivation, while need-supportive teaching may work more reliably through motivation than through a uniform direct achievement effect.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 reading-focused data for 15-year-olds across 76 regions (after excluding Canada, Lebanon, and Northern Macedonia) and groups them into Schwartz’s eight cultural value orientations. It models perceived need-supportive teaching (NST) as a three-item latent construct and uses reading intrinsic motivation as the mediator, with reading achievement represented by PISA’s ten plausible values. Using PISA’s complex sampling approach (80 replicate weights) and multiple imputation for missingness (<6% per case), the SEM results show that intrinsic motivation positively predicts reading achievement across all eight cultures, with the largest standardized paths reported in the range of about 0.24–0.42. The indirect pathway from NST to achievement via intrinsic motivation is statistically significant across all eight groups but with small effect sizes, while the direct NST→achievement link is only partially supported. The authors emphasize that PISA is cross-sectional, so causal claims are limited, and the study relies on self-reported teaching perceptions rather than objective classroom observations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is an SEM-based cross-cultural mediation test using PISA plausible values and survey replicate weights; it does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models. As a result, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty (no ML algorithms are reported), and the extraction focuses on the substantive SEM path results rather than predictive accuracy metrics.
